title: I made two games, one 100% with AI and one I spent a year on. Can you tell the difference?
author: FarPlace9870
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I've made two mobile games in pretty different ways and wanted to share both.

The first one is ZeroPath, and it's 100% made with AI. I didn't write a single line of code myself, I just wanted to see how far you could get that way. It's a number puzzle: you drag your finger across the squares, each one you pass over goes down by one, and you have to get them all to zero in a single stroke. It has 11 worlds, each adding a new mechanic, plus daily challenges with a global leaderboard. Here's the link: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.zeropath.game

The second one, Tilt Jump, is my baby. It was my idea and I spent a year developing it. The only part I did with AI was the UI, because design really isn't my thing and I'd rather focus on everything else. You play it by tilting your phone: sideways to move, more upright to jump higher, and you tap to jump through the gaps between pipes, which of course won't stay still. It has 300 levels, a survival mode, 1v1 multiplayer and 18 characters, each with its own ability. You can get it here: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sefotud.tiltjump

I'd really appreciate it if you gave them a try, especially the second one. And if you notice a big difference between the two, I'd like to hear about that too.

Criticism is welcome, that's what I'm posting for.

comments.author: Luxurious-Shirt
comments.body: does dragging back over a square you already zeroed push it negative or does it just stay put?

replies.author: FarPlace9870
replies.body: Neither, actually. Once a square hits zero it's blocked and you can't go over it again, so you really have to plan your path. If you mess up, you can always use a hint that lets you cross a zeroed square to get to another part of the board. And if you drag back along your own path, it just undoes the move
